newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says Rwanda and Burundi back infiltrators.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says Rwanda and Burundi back infiltrators.

text.p: Zaire said on Friday its troops had clashed with armed groups of Banyamulenge Tutsi infiltrators and accused neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi of raising tension in the region by backing the cross-border raids.

A government statement said the infiltrators had killed people in the east and that the aim of the incursions, from Rwanda via Burundi, was to stir up already hostile relations between Banyamulenge settled in Zaire and locals.
Government officials also reported a seperate incursion into Zaire from Uganda during which 13 people were killed.

"The Banyamulenge have been responsible for several violations of Zairean territory which have resulted in the deaths of Zairean men since the beginning of the month," the government statement said, confirming clashes with troops in Uvira region near Burundi. It gave no precise death tolls.

The government "denounces and energetically condemns the behaviour of Rwanda and Burundi, who, through their participation in the Banyamulenge aggression against Zaire, breach existing accords", it added.

Volatile eastern Zaire is host to a million Rwandan Hutus who fled fearing reprisals following 1994 massacres by Hutu hardliners in Rwanda of minority-Tutsis and the civil war victory of Tutsi-led rebels.
The Zairean statement said 3,000 Banyamulenge had been repatriated to Rwanda last year and had joined the Rwandan army with a view to destabilising eastern Zaire.
Burundi radio said on Thursday that Zairean troops were persecuting Zairean nationals, calling them Rwandan Tutsis. It quoted refugees crossing the border.

The Zairean statement, signed by Interior Minister Gerard Kamanda wa Kamanda, drew the attention of the U.N. secretary-general and Security Council to "the behaviour on the ground of certain member states who accentuate and make worse insecurity in the Great Lakes region".
He also urged the United States and other Western states to take up the matter with Rwanda and Burundi.
The statement quoted infiltrators as saying that they had been helped by United Nations and other relief agencies and the Rwandan, Burundian and Ugandan armies.

Zairean officials said 13 people had been killed on Thursday when an armed band who crossed from Uganda opened fire on a village on the border. A Zairean soldier and two security agents were among the dead. The attackers took flight.
A government spokesman said Zaire protested vigorously against Uganda's unfriendly behaviour.
Zaire and Rwandan agreed last month during a visit by Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo to Kigali to repatriate the Rwandan refugees before Zairean elections planned for May.
